title.value: W. M. Keck Observatory parameters for the observing-night simulator + ETC
title.note: Compiled 2026-09-24. confidence: documented = stated in the cited source; approximate = derived by arithmetic from documented numbers, read from a data file by me, secondary source, or older/proxy measurement; estimate = not found publicly, reasoned value (see note).

scratch_note.value: Pages fetched live 2026-09-24; CFHT pages via web.archive.org (live site returns 403).

name.value: W. M. Keck Observatory, Maunakea, Hawaii

longitude_deg.note: Keck guide (2002): 155d28.4m W. IRAF/astropy 'keck' entry: 204.521667 E = -155.478333.

elevation_m.note: Keck guide (2002) altitude. IRAF/astropy 'keck' entry uses 4160 m; commonly quoted 4145 m. Differences are below what matters for an ETC.

astropy_keck_site.note: Source field in the registry: 'IRAF Observatory Database'. Use EarthLocation.of_site('keck').

telescope_separation_m.note: Keck II lies roughly NE of Keck I.

timezone.note: FACSUM: UT is '10 hours ahead of HST'.

mean_pressure_mbar.note: CFHT manual: unit airmass at Maunakea equals 0.60 sea-level airmasses. Read via web.archive.org; the live page returns 403.

night_temperature_C.note: TMT 13N median night temperature at 2 m: 2.3 C.

median_wind_speed_m_s.note: Keck guide: ~7 m/s (~14 mph). CFHT: 50% < 7 m/s, 84% < 12 m/s, about 5% > 30 m/s (telescope closed).

pwv_median_mm.note: TMT 13N site (4050 m): median 1.9 mm, and PWV < 2 mm 54% of the time. The CFHT manual quotes a median of 0.9 mm (older, summit).

usable_night_fraction.note: CFHT manual (2003). Gemini treats its 50th-percentile cloud-cover bin at MK as 'photometric' (no signal loss).

note.value: Pick one table consistently. For optical ETC work in AB, use the MegaCam values. Use the Gemini percentiles to model the lunar phase, and the MOSFIRE tables for NIR spectroscopy between OH lines.

u.note: CFHT MegaCam, zenith, Moon 0%. Read via web.archive.org.

g.note: CFHT MegaCam, zenith, Moon 0%. Read via web.archive.org.

B.note: CFHT Observatory Manual Sec. 2, 'average sky brightness at zenith during dark time'.

V_incl_OI.note: 'various estimates that probably include the OI line'.

SB20_darkest.note: <=3 nights from new moon. U=V+0.0, B=V+0.8, R=V-0.9.

random_target_median.note: Fainter than 20.78 for 50% of the time and than 21.37 for 20% of the time, for a random target.

ecliptic_penalty.note: V sky ~0.4 mag brighter at low ecliptic latitude.

J.note: Gemini Maunakea near-IR background, any lunar phase.

H.note: Gemini Maunakea near-IR background, any lunar phase.

K.note: Gemini Maunakea near-IR background, any lunar phase.

Y.note: MOSFIRE imaging. SPIE 2012 range 17.37-17.50 Vega (full moon).

Ks.note: SPIE range 13.68-14.25. Includes telescope thermal emission.

Y.note: 0.7 arcsec slit, per spatial pixel, between OH lines. Measured during full moon.

mosfire_band_avg_spec_sky_AB_derived.note: My flux-average of the MOSFIRE night-sky FITS spectra (data/MosfireSkyspec/*_abmag.fits), linked from sky_lines.html.

airmass_scaling.value: sky brightness ~ proportional to airmass (first approximation)

nir_oh_variability.note: OH declines steadily for the first 1-2 h after sunset. MOSFIRE team: OH lines vary by >0.1% on ~30 s timescales.

u.note: CFHT MegaCam photometric airmass term k.

g.note: CFHT MegaCam photometric airmass term k.

r.note: CFHT MegaCam photometric airmass term k.

i.note: CFHT MegaCam photometric airmass term k.

z.note: CFHT MegaCam photometric airmass term k.

U.note: n=1 only. Krisciunas et al. 1987 (PASP 99, 887), Dec 1980 to May 1996 compilation.

J.note: Old UKIRT J filter. Much higher than MKO-filter values.
Tokunaga, Simons & Vacca 2002, as tabulated by Gemini, for 2 mm PWV.

buton2013_median_curve.note: SNfactory median, 3200-10000 A in 100 A bins (A&A 549, A8, Table 6). Continuum only: add O2/H2O telluric bands separately. Variability rms is ~0.057 mag/airmass at 3300 A and ~0.003 at 9000 A.

mkam_dimm_median.note: MKAM DIMM (between CFHT and Gemini-N), 2009-2020, Lyman et al. 2020 mean/median table. Read from the MNRAS HTML through a text-extraction fetch because the PDF host was unreachable; two independent fetches agreed. The text also calls 0.65 arcsec the typical total seeing.

mkam_ground_layer_median.note: Mean 0.47. The ground layer is 2/3 to 3/4 of the total seeing. Same retrieval caveat.

tmt13n_dimm_median.note: TMT 13N (4050 m, ~150 m below summit, 7 m DIMM height). 10th percentile 0.46.

dimm_quartiles.note: No published quartile table found. Lognormal with median 0.65 (MKAM) and sigma_ln = 0.38. sigma_ln comes from the TMT 13N 10%/50% ratio: 0.46/0.75 gives sigma = -ln(0.613)/1.2816. The implied P(>1.5 arcsec) is ~1.4%, consistent with Marcy+2014 (<10%).

seeing_gt_1p5_fraction.note: Stated in passing in Marcy et al. 2014 (HIRES).

keck2_visible_median.note: 'approximately the median for the Keck 2 telescope' (LGS AO page).

keck_telescope_optics_EE.value: 80% of energy within 0.4 arcsec diameter; FWHM ~0.2 arcsec
keck_telescope_optics_EE.note: Segment + f/15 secondary + tertiary optical quality. Add in quadrature to the seeing.

deimos_good.note: 'FWHM=0.5 arcsec is achievable under good seeing conditions'.

gemini_mk_iq_percentiles_zenith.note: Delivered IQ at Gemini-N (8 m), a good proxy for Keck.

airmass_scaling.value: FWHM proportional to airmass^0.6 (visible and short-wave IR)

wavelength_scaling.note: Standard Kolmogorov scaling, not quoted by a Keck page. The Gemini IQ table is roughly consistent with it.

seasonal.note: June and September have the most nights with total seeing < 0.6 arcsec.

policy_note.value: Guidelines only. The Observing Assistant has ultimate authority.

wind_close.value: sustained 45 mph; OR sustained >=25 mph with moderate dust accumulation

wind_reopen.value: sustained <=40 mph for >=30 min, gusts <45 mph, minimal dust after a 30-min buildup test, no other adverse weather

wind_limit_2002_guide.note: Older guide: 'allowable wind velocity with dome open: 50 mph', which may vary with dust and dome orientation.

dewpoint_close.value: dewpoint within 2 C of the outside, secondary or primary-mirror temperature, sustained 5 min; or condensation on outside surfaces
dewpoint_close.note: Humidity is enforced through the dew-point margin; the table gives no RH%.

dewpoint_reopen.value: dewpoint margin >2 C for >=30 min (precip/condensation) or >=20 min (fog) AND no condensation buildup after 30 min

fog_close.value: fog sighted within 200 m of telescope; or within 400 m and within 15 min of contact; sudden dewpoint jump

fog_reopen.value: no fog or clouds within 400 m of domes, no low clouds within 1/2 mile of summit, plus dewpoint rule

precipitation_close.value: any visible precipitation; stratus/cumulus clouds overhead of the domes

high_clouds_close.value: precipitation-producing clouds overhead; or cloud >6 mag extinction AND conditions preclude the primary program

ice_snow_on_dome.value: close/do not open if ice or snow has accumulated on the dome, or snow falls in when opening; reopen when winds are sustained <10 mph with no infalling material

relative_humidity_limit.note: Not on the Keck table. van Kooten & Izett 2022 model the Keck criteria as U < 20 m/s, RH < 95% and T - Tdew > 2 K. Use it as an operational proxy.

closure_statistics.note: From Keck records cited by van Kooten & Izett 2022. Interpret with care.

recommended_for_etc.note: 72.295 m^2: 'net usable primary area in the f/15 configuration with the baffles retracted' (Nelson 1994, cited by J. Cohen on the LRIS efficiency page).

perley2019.note: 'physical area of the primary mirror (73.3 m2)', LPipe paper.

lris_zp_1994.note: 0.97*pi*(10 m)^2/4, used for the 1994 LRIS zero points (0.97 for the central hole).

mirror_reflectivity.note: Loss budget in Perley 2019 (from Oke et al. 1995). The LRIS-B page says multiply by ~0.8 for the telescope.

azimuth_convention.value: azimuth from North through East (N=0, E=90)
azimuth_convention.note: Inferred: the K1 deck range 5-146 deg is described as 'North and East' and the K2 range 185-333 deg as 'South and West'.

practical_lower_el_deg.note: Unvignetted limit outside the deck zone. From 0 to 18 deg the beam is vignetted.

guiding_upper_el_deg.note: 'Stable guiding cannot be guaranteed for targets transiting at elevations higher than ~85 deg'.

mosfire_guiding_limits.note: Guiding degrades above these. Between 87 and 88 deg the MOSFIRE team stopped guiding.

az_slew_rate_deg_s.note: Also quoted in the NIRC manual.

pointing_accuracy_arcsec_rms.note: 2002 value; current pointing is likely better.

slew_settle_s.note: No settle time is published. The NIRC manual says a small offset plus guider settle takes ~6 s, and a full acquisition ~5 min. Use 10-20 s for servo settle after a large slew, before guide-star acquisition.

dome_rotation.value: assume dome keeps pace with the azimuth slew (~1 deg/s)
dome_rotation.note: No public dome rotation rate found. Assume the dome is not the bottleneck except on >90 deg azimuth moves.

rotator_ranges.note: DEIMOS from its specs page; MOSFIRE from McLean+2012 SPIE.

typical_acquisition_s.note: 'Including a typical slew, identifying the field, centering, and sending to the science detector, a round number to use is 5 minutes for an acquisition' (Keck NIRC manual). The rotator can move during the slew, and the instrument can be reconfigured.

small_offset_plus_guide_settle_s.note: 'Offsetting the telescope includes the actual move plus the time it takes for the guiding to settle. This is typically 6 sec.'

focus_mira_s.note: 'Wait about 10 minutes for the OA to acquire an appropriate star and run Mira.' The MOSFIRE SAT page recommends refocusing when elevation has changed by 30 deg or more since the last focus.

faint_longslit_acquisition_s.note: Estimated from the documented LRIS/DEIMOS blind-offset procedure after the ~5-min slew/acquire: a 30 s slit image and a 30 s field image, each plus ~50-90 s readout, a mov/movb offset, an optional confirmation image, a slit re-insert and a focus change. That sums to ~6-12 min. Use 10 min (plus 5 min slew).

slitmask_alignment_s.note: DEIMOS ~5 min is documented (DEEP2: 'generally converges after two direct images and takes roughly 5 minutes'). LRIS and MOSFIRE are estimates. MOSFIRE mask execution (<6 min) can run during the slew, then coarse + fine align. LRIS readouts are longer; aligning with blue-side images saves 35-45 min per night per Steidel.

value: vertical angle mode (slit follows parallactic when set to 0)
rotator_modes.note: Long bright on-slit guiding: vertical angle 0. Short offset-guided exposures: PA mode at the current parallactic angle. Long offset-guided: PA = parallactic angle at mid-exposure.

example.value: dec +40, HA 2h east -> parallactic angle 60 deg

night_definition.note: Keck Duty-Cycle Metrics: 'The time between 12 deg twilights is the formal definition of the night.' Split nights are divided at the midpoint between 12 deg twilights.

split_night_rule.value: first-half observers finish their last exposure at the midpoint
split_night_rule.note: LRIS/DEIMOS cannot be reconfigured at night. Split-night PIs submit one shared configuration.

instrument_reconfig_at_night.value: LRIS gratings / DEIMOS gratings / HIRES cross-disperser fixed for the night
instrument_reconfig_at_night.note: HIRES b<->r XD swap is never done at night (blue_vs_red page). LRIS/DEIMOS gratings come from the configuration form.

wavelength_range_A.note: Blue arm ~3100-6000 (optimized), red arm via dichroic.

peak_system_efficiency.note: 'peak system efficiencies of ~50%' (home page). The home page does not say what is included; the efficiency pages quote instrument+CCD only (no telescope/atmosphere).

dichroics.note: D500 is 4800 in one column of the table; D680 is 6640/6800. Transmission >95%, reflection >98% outside the transition.

status_note.value: Red CCD Mark IV (4k x 4k LBNL) installed April/May 2021

full_well_e.note: Derived: linear limit 62000 ADU x 1.55-1.70 e-/ADU = 96k-105k e-. ADC-limited.

dark_current_e_per_hr.note: Not published. Typical of LN2-cooled E2V CCDs; negligible compared with sky.

type.value: LBNL 4k x 4k, 500 um deep-depletion, 15 um pixels (Mark IV)

dark_current_e_per_hr.note: Not published. A thick LBNL CCD at about -100 C: assume a few e-/pix/hr.

readout_s.note: Detector-page value. The mode-specific table is below.

binning_modes.note: Set with 'lredccd_setup imag|spec <bx> <by>'. Imaging uses 4 amps, spectroscopy 2 amps.

blue_spatial_window_100pix_1x1.note: Spatial windowing does not save time on blue.

red_4amp_1x1.note: Elapsed for a 0-s exposure, including erase, expose and readout.

instrument_efficiency.note: Mirror in place of dichroic; instrument + CCD, excluding telescope and atmosphere. Data from 2002.

system_efficiency_peak_with_telescope.note: 0.49 x 0.8 ('to get total system throughput including the telescope, multiply by about 0.8').

coverage_A.note: Detector coverage. Usable >~3100 A (atmosphere) and <~7000 A (blue camera).

instrument_efficiency_peak.note: '300/5000 grism provides a peak efficiency of about 56%'. The data file gives 0.55 at 5000 A.

red_old_ccd_peaks_excl_tel_atm.note: 1995 measurement with the ORIGINAL Tek red CCD. Instrument + CCD only.

red_400/8500_total_peak.note: No current curve is published for the Mark IV CCD. Estimate: ~0.38-0.40 instrument peak (similar to the 600/7500 old measurement; the Mark IV has 'similar QE' to the previous LBNL mosaic, which was much redder-sensitive than the Tek) x 0.76 telescope. Beyond 9000 A LRIS beats DEIMOS.

effective_area_observed.note: Includes atmosphere, telescope, slit losses; clear weather, average seeing; over optimal-sensitivity region of each grism/grating (Perley 2019).

loss_budget_6000A.note: Typical conditions, after Oke et al. 1995.

red_max_single_s.note: 'we recommend maximum exposure times of 20 minutes to avoid excessive contamination by cosmic rays' (Mark IV).

blue_typical_mask_exposure_s.note: Steidel+2004 LBG masks: 3 x 1800 s, dithered 1-2 arcsec along the slit.

blue_element_change_s.note: Dichroic, grism or filter change '<60 seconds'.

red_grating_change.note: The DEIMOS primer says its grating change is 'comparable to the time required for an LRIS grating change'. Use 300 s.

red_grating_tilt_change_s.note: Not published. Grating-angle moves on this class of stage take tens of seconds.

red_filter_or_slitmask_change_s.note: Not published. The red side moves 2 mechanisms at once (grating + slitmask/filter/focus).

faint_target_procedure.value: 30 s slit image; 30 s direct image; movb/movr offset; optional confirm; refocus MIRA/AUTOFOC

old_red_AB20_count_rate.note: 1995, OLD Tek CCD with 24 um pixels. Use the efficiencies, not these per-pixel rates.

imaging_zeropoints_1994.note: Mean of two nights, 1.72 e-/DN, ORIGINAL red CCD. Historical; recalibrate for Mark IV.

max_slitlets.note: Up to 130 slitlets with 1.5 arcsec gaps; tilted slits up to 30 deg.

filters.note: An order-blocking or broadband filter must always be in.

measured_2018_incl_telescope.note: Nd/Nt: photons detected over photons hitting the primary (atmosphere removed). Sampled from the ECSV tables (ripisc/<grating>/*.txt), 2010-2018 standards (T. Lai).

spec_page_prediction_6000A.note: Predicted (CCD QE 0.6, silver coatings). The primer says the total peaks near 30%.

deep2_exposures.value: 3 x 1200 s per mask, no dithering

mirror_grating_mode_change_s.note: '120-190 sec changeover between mirror and grating, depending on slider'.

grating_change.note: The primer recommends zeroth-order imaging (GO ZERO / GO BACK) for alignment instead of swapping to the mirror.

zeroth_order_tilt_s.note: Not published. A grating tilt move plus FCS re-lock.

fcs_lock_s.note: 'It may take a couple of minutes for the FCS to lock.'

mask_alignment_s.note: DEEP2: converges after two direct images, ~5 min, and is re-checked once after the first exposure.

slitmask_change_s.note: Not published. Can be done during the slew.

spec_prediction_600l.note: Point source, 0.75 arcsec slit, 0.7 arcsec seeing, 5500 A, 0.65 A/px, V sky 21.25 mag/arcsec^2. V is the magnitude through the slit (predicted).

achieved_1200G_faint_galaxies.note: 1.0 arcsec slit, ~7000 A, 0.32 A/px, average conditions, total mag (no slit-loss correction).

deep2_1200G_1hr.unit: R_AB -> [Q1, median, Q3] S/N per pixel in 1 h
deep2_1200G_1hr.note: ~50,000 DEEP2 galaxies, 1200G, 6600-6830 and 6960-7250 A, 1 arcsec slits. Galaxies are extended, so point sources do better.

fov_arcmin.note: Corners vignetted; the collimator field is 6.8 arcmin.

slits.note: Configurable Slit Unit; any width. Recipes assume 0.7 arcsec.

csu_reconfig_s.note: 'Reconfiguration time is < 6 minutes' (SPIE). The home page says 'under 5 minutes'.

status_note.note: Check availability for simulated dates after Aug 2026.

read_noise_e.note: SPIE: CDS 23.2 e- at the telescope.

persistence.note: The persistence page says e-folding ~10-12 min (<1% after 51 min). 'When in doubt, go dark.'

min_integration_s.note: Exposure times are quantized by 1.455 s.

mcds_overhead_s.note: MCDS8 11.6 s, MCDS16 23.3 s, MCDS32 46.6 s.

optimal_exposure_s.note: For targets fainter than the sky.

dither_patterns.note: Default dither space 2.5 arcsec at design; 1.5 arcsec nod, 3 arcsec A-B separation.

csu_fatal_error.note: Rate from the 2025-04-29 news table. Suggested move elevation ~67 deg.

mode_change_s.note: Filter-wheel/pupil/grating move is not quantified (SPIE: filter-wheel cycle ~2x spec). Assume 60-120 s, overlapped with 'Wait & Go'.

pa_definitions.note: To put a longslit N-S, set ROTDEST = -4.00.

mosdef_3sigma_continuum_per_pixel_2hr.unit: AB mag range, per pixel (typ. ~2 h/filter, 60-245 min; seeing 0.5-0.8 arcsec)
mosdef_3sigma_continuum_per_pixel_2hr.note: Kriek+2015 Table 1, total (slit-loss corrected), point source. The MOSFIRE ETC is optimistic by ~2x.

steidel2014_5sigma_line_1hr.note: As quoted by Kriek+2015; not slit-loss corrected

coverage_per_exposure_A.note: Complete coverage shortward of 6200 A. Longer wavelengths need 2 settings.

image_rotator.value: optional; holds slit at a PA or at parallactic

iodine_cell_and_exposure_meter.note: Exposure meter PMT 300-650 nm; the pick-off costs 1% of the light.

gain_low_e_per_adu.note: Spec page lists 1.9, 2.2, 2.2. Low gain is the default.

full_well_e_low_gain.note: Derived: 39800 ADU x 1.95. Nonlinearity becomes significant above ~half full well (ccdgain page).

spatial_scale_arcsec.note: 'about 0.12 arcseconds on the sky, in the spatial direction'

dispersion_A_per_pix_5500.note: Derived from 1.3 km/s x 5500 A / c.

deckers.unit: [slit width arcsec, R calculated, R measured UV-XD]
deckers.note: Lengths 3.5-28 arcsec by decker (B1 3.5, B2 7, B3 14, B4 28, C2 14, ...). The red-XD measured R is ~1% higher.

measured_page.note: Slitless 4x5 arcsec decker; no tabulated values.

total_peak_incl_telescope.note: My back-of-envelope from the Marcy+2014 anchor. The observed ~2% end-to-end includes the iodine cell, 0.86 arcsec slit losses and atmosphere; correcting those gives ~5-8%. Vogt+1994 (pre-2004 CCD) is ~8% near 6000 A per secondary summaries.

typical_long_exposure_s.note: 'typical long exposures of 10-45 minutes' (CPS / Kepler follow-up)

setup_changes.value: echelle/XD angle changes by software; XD swap impossible at night

exposure_meter_warmup_s.note: 'allow at least 10 minutes for the PMT to warm up'.

cps_kepler.note: 'at Kp = 13.0 mag, the typical exposure was 45 minutes, giving SNR=75 per pixel'

bandpass_nm.note: The red arm (KCRM) works simultaneously; dichroic at 560 nm.

slicers.note: R scales 1x : 2x : 4x for L : M : S.

gratings.note: Red values are lab measurements (unbinned pixels). Nod-and-shuffle cuts the bandpass by ~4x.

readout_s.note: Blue 2-amp slow is the common mode. Do not use quad-amp with N&S.

exposure_limits.note: Blue exposures can only be shortened in progress; red can be lengthened or shortened.

note.value: pre-ship and commissioning curves published only as plots
note.note: Commissioning curves include atmosphere at airmass 1 and 3 reflections; instrument alone is ~0.2 higher.

total_peak_BL_BM.note: Estimate: instrument ~0.45-0.5 at peak x telescope 0.8 x atmosphere 0.85. BH3 is ~25% below the others.

note.value: no numeric S/N anchor found on public pages
note.note: Use the KCWI ETC linked from the KCWI pages.

show.note: 'show -s <service> keywords' lists all keywords. -terse returns the bare value (for scripts).

modify.note: Blocks until the move completes unless nowait. Scripts also use 'silent' (e.g. modify -s dcs silent raoff=..).

services.note: LRIS/ACS/DCS: cl.html; DEIMOS: deimos-keyword-summary.html; MOSFIRE: mosfire_keywords.html; HIRES: troublepage.html (show -s hiccd ..., show -s hires lfilname). On DEIMOS/K2 hosts the telescope service is also addressed as 'dcs' (DEIMOS scripts).

en_radec.value: modify -s dcs silent raoff=<E_arcsec> decoff=<N_arcsec> rel2curr=t

azel.value: modify -s dcs silent azoff=<arcsec> eloff=<arcsec> rel2curr=t

mxy_instrument.value: modify -s dcs silent instxoff=<x> instyoff=<y> rel2curr=t  (rel2base=t variant exists)

dome_flats_flag.note: Tells the summit crew not to enter the dome.

wftel.value: wftel: wait for telescope move / guider resume (polls dcs AUTACTIV, AUTRESUM, AUTGO)

keywords.note: The list predates the 2021 Mark IV red CCD. Red exposures are now driven by scripts (tintr/goir/abortr); the red-CCD keyword names may differ.

scripts.note: Also redccdmanual.html, dither.html, shell_scripts.html (csh example uses tintr, tintb, goibr, goir, goib, lamps, slit, grating -mswave).

value.goi [-nowait] [-dark] [N]: take N exposures (expose=t, then waitfor wcrate/wserv/wdisk)

scripts.note: Typical science start from the checklist: 'wffcs ; goi'.

value.MOSFIRE.ITIME: integration time per coadd in ms
value.MOSFIRE.ABORT: 1 now, 2 after read, 3 after group, 4 after coadd
value.MOSFIRE.CSUREADY: CSU state (2 ready, 3 moving, 4 configuring, -1 error)
value.MDS.* / MCSUS.*: detector / CSU servers mirror the same names

value.Quick Dark / Wait & Go (GUI): dark filter / start sequence after mechanisms

value.hiccd: CCD (e.g. show -s hiccd dwrxfrsw; modify -s hiccd autofill=1)

services.note: No public HIRES exposure keyword list found; exposure keywords not confirmed here.

scripts.note: Red-side equivalents exist (framer, nextfiler, ...), but red exposure-script names were not seen in the public list.
